name: pickup-spawn
demonstrates: PickupManager schedules the first pickup spawn ~8s after a run begins (per PickupManagerTests) and each pickup persists for a ~20s lifetime, placed on a street tile clear of adjacent buildings (per the placement-search rules pinned by PickupIntegrationTests). This journey waits ~12s past PLAY (past the 8s first-spawn delay with margin for the placement search and frame timing) and takes a screenshot labelled pickup-spawned, reviewed for a small bobbing med-kit or garbage-can icon rendered over an accent-tinted pad -- the tint sits on the pad only, never on the icon itself -- sitting on a street tile and depth-sorted correctly next to any nearby building (not overlapping or drawn behind it), with med kits and garbage cans visually distinguishable from one another. It then waits a further ~6s (now ~18s past PLAY, inside the pickup's lifetime window and past a plausible player-collection window) and takes a second screenshot labelled pickup-lifecycle, reviewed to confirm the pickup is still on the street and still bobbing ~6s later -- the same pickup that spawned at ~8s, or a cleared pad if the player happened to collect it in between -- rather than a sprite that vanishes the moment after it appears. Recurrence and replacement are deliberately NOT claimed for this frame: by the cadence arithmetic below, no second spawn can occur before ~PLAY+33s, so these two screenshots necessarily show the same pickup ~6s apart; that the scheduler keeps producing further pickups after the first is pinned by PickupManagerTests, not observable in these frames. That second wait targets ~18s rather than the ~22s an earlier draft used, because the frozen numbers in PickupKind.tuningTable leave a recurring EMPTY window that a later frame can fall into: cadence (25s) is longer than lifetime (20s) and a kind's cadence re-arms only after a successful spawn, so the effective ceiling is one pickup at a time -- the first pickup expires at ~PLAY+28s and the next one cannot appear before ~PLAY+33s (see the PickupKind.Tuning.maxAlive doc note). navigate is vision-located and each wait starts only after the previous step returns, so ~18s keeps roughly 10s of cumulative slop in hand before that 28-33s dead zone. A reviewer who still lands on an empty street in this frame should read it as that timing artifact rather than as a regression. Camera-independence is explicitly NOT claimed by these screenshots: no step here moves the camera (this journey's action vocabulary is wait / assert_running / screenshot / navigate), so the player stands at the spawn junction for the whole run and the frames cannot distinguish "lifetime is aged by deltaTime only" from "the pickup survived because the camera never moved". That property -- a pickup is never deleted merely because the camera moved -- is pinned by PickupManagerTests.test_largeVisibleRectJumpBetweenUpdates_doesNotAffectPickupAging, which teleports visibleRect a million points between two update calls and asserts expiry still lands on real accumulated deltaTime. Gate is human/vision review of both screenshots; assert_running steps only confirm the app process is still alive. The underlying spawn timing, placement rules, bobbing/tinted rendering, collection and depth-sort behavior are already pinned by PickupManagerTests, PickupNodeTests, PickupIntegrationTests, RaccoonPickupDiversionTests and PlayerHealTests -- this journey exists purely so the runtime probe captures frames late enough for a pickup to actually be on screen, instead of the menu-to-gameplay journey's 5s screenshot which fires well before the first pickup can possibly exist. TWO PROBE RUNS HAVE INSTEAD REPORTED THE APP PROCESS GONE right around PLAY+12s and PLAY+18s, i.e. shortly after PickupKind.medKit/garbageCan's shared 8s firstSpawnDelay fires -- the moment the first Pickup record is created and the first PickupNode is mounted into GameScene -- with two independent static audits of PickupManager/PickupNode/PickupKind/AtlasSheet.pickups/DepthBanding/GameScene's pickup wiring/RaccoonSeekBehavior's diversion path finding no reachable crash site. Rather than re-adding a signal-handler crash-capture harness (tried once already on the near-identical CYBERPUN-17-10 pulse-ability crash: shipped, then removed at close-out as un-owned scaffolding once its own named removal ticket was never filed, with the crash still unidentified -- see the CYBERPUN-17-10/CYBERPUN-17-11 entries in CLAUDE.md), the original 12s/18s single waits are now SPLIT so assert_running brackets the 8s delay: wait 4 (PLAY+4s, before the delay can fire) -> assert_running -> wait 4 (PLAY+8s, the delay fires -- first Pickup created / first PickupNode mounted) -> assert_running -> wait 4 (back to the original PLAY+12s) -> screenshot pickup-spawned -> assert_running -> wait 6 (PLAY+18s) -> screenshot pickup-lifecycle -> assert_running. Total elapsed time and both screenshot timings are UNCHANGED from before; only the bisection checkpoints are new. The 'before' checkpoint sits at PLAY+4s rather than PLAY+7s deliberately (PR #61 review): the two clocks do not start at the same instant -- firstSpawnDelay starts ticking when .gameplay is entered, at the moment the PLAY tap lands, while these waits start only when the vision-located navigate step RETURNS, i.e. after the probe has verified its expect state -- so a nominal PLAY+7s checkpoint can fire at real PLAY+8.5s once the ~10s of cumulative slop this paragraph already budgets starts accruing, and a 'process gone' there would be misreported as 'died before pickups are even touched' when the first Pickup may already exist. 4s of nominal margin keeps that arm discriminating; the 3s came out of the following wait (1 -> 4), so both screenshot timings and total elapsed time are still exactly what they were. This does not fix or even localize the crash -- it narrows what the NEXT 'process gone' report can say: died before the delay ever fires (nothing pickup-related is even reached), died right as the first pickup is created/mounted (implicates that exact code path), or survived past it (implicates something later, e.g. player collection or a second update tick). JourneyManifestTests.test_thePickupSpawnJourney_bisectsTheFirstSpawnDelayWithAssertRunningCheckpoints pins both checkpoints against PickupKind.medKit.tuning.firstSpawnDelay: the 'before' checkpoint must land strictly under the delay, and the FIRST checkpoint at or after it must land inside a narrow window (delay .. delay+2s) rather than merely existing somewhere later. The window is what makes the gate bind: the pre-existing assert_running steps after each screenshot already sit at 12s and 18s, both at-or-after the 8s delay, so an 'exists somewhere later' assertion would pass vacuously and deleting the tight checkpoint would keep the suite green. With the window, deleting either checkpoint -- or a retune of firstSpawnDelay that moves it away from these waits -- fails in-suite instead of silently losing the bisection. SCAFFOLDING(TBD -- root-cause ticket, filed by the gate reviewer): the two bracketing assert_running checkpoints and the JourneyManifestTests gate that pins them are diagnostic instrumentation for a still-unidentified crash, not permanent journey shape. No ticket ID is invented here because filing the root-cause ticket is the human call AGENT.md records as outstanding; whoever files it should write its ID into this marker and the matching one on that test, and when it closes BOTH checkpoints and that test are removed, leaving the journey's original 12s/18s waits.

steps.target: the large neon-outlined PLAY button in the middle of the title screen that starts a new run (NOT the plain HIGH SCORES button below it)
steps.expect: the running game -- a playable isometric city scene with a ground lattice, buildings and a player actor, not a menu or title screen
